key_insight: CARing improves next-visit diagnosis prediction by combining semantic ID tokens for diagnoses with a coverage-based learning objective so the model covers more valid diagnoses instead of repeatedly predicting the same few.
clinical_relevance: This could support more complete automated support for multi-label diagnosis prediction from longitudinal EHRs, especially when multiple diagnoses may all be correct for a patient.
method: Represents ICD-style diagnoses as compact compositional Semantic IDs (SIDs) using residual quantization.
Aligns SID tokens with natural language and longitudinal EHR context through multi-task alignment and reasoning-enriched training.
Uses coverage reward plus multi-positive supervision, with direct constrained decoding or multi-chain reasoning at inference.
evidence_signal: On MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV, the method outperformed EHR-trained baselines in weighted F1 and achieved the highest top-k recall, including R@30 of 46.04% and 46.52% in reasoning mode.
watch_item: Performance is reported on retrospective benchmark datasets, so clinical deployment would still need external validation, calibration, and workflow testing for safety and robustness.
paper_title: Coverage-Aware Reasoning with Medical Tokens for Diagnosis Prediction
